1 Samuel 20 · David's Empty Seat at the New Moon
The Feasts of the Most High

points: David hid himself in the field, and when the new moon was come the king sat down to eat. David fled at the first of the month, and at the new moon meal his seat was empty.

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: That first day Saul spake not anything, for he thought something had befallen David, that surely he was not clean; but on the second day of the month, with David's place empty again, Saul asked Jonathan, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat?

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: Saul got wind that his own son was hiding David out. When Jonathan covered for David, Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan: as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom.

note.label: 1 Samuel 20: David's Empty Seat at the New Moon

points: Saul cast a javelin at Jonathan to smite him, whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David; from here the history follows Saul pursuing David.
